posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Gavin Baker (@GavinSBaker) on orbital compute:

"The most important thing in the next 3-4 years is data centers in space.

In space, you can keep a satellite in the sun 24 hours a day. So you don't need a battery. Space cooling is free.

In every way, data centers in space, from a first principles perspective, are superior to data centers on earth."

"@elonmusk operates two of the largest coherent GPU clusters in the world, SpaceX is responsible for over 90% of mass to orbit and SpaceX operates the largest satellite constellation in the solar system. 

More than 10 years later, no other company or country can consistently land and reuse orbital rockets."

"Starship should be able to lift 10 to 15 megawatts to sun-synchronous orbit per flight."

"Starship is going to change the space economy in ways we cannot imagine.

Particularly if regulation becomes a constraint to data centers, none of it's going to matter. You're going to sell as much orbital compute as you can make."

A collection of Gavin's quotes from his conversations on Invest Like the Best (EP.451 and EP.473) and his own posts on X.

quote.author: cb_doge

quote.text:
Starlink helped save FIVE lives in the Atlantic. ♥️

Their boat, Karolina Viking, was filling with water. Its power systems were failing. Rescuers couldn’t reach them by radio or satellite phone.

The sailors shared their location with rescuers through Starlink, helping another yacht find them.

All five were rescued from their liferaft and brought safely aboard.

Starlink helped turn a desperate situation into five lives saved. This is what a lifeline from space looks like.

Yeah, much easier to cool in space. 

~1300 W/m^2 is easily achievable for an aluminum radiator pointed away from the Sun, as it is mostly just seeing cosmic background radiation at ~3 degrees above absolute zero!

Solar panels generate ~250 W/m^2, so you should expect them to have ~5 times the area of the radiator. Most of the mass of the satellite is solar panels.

Steven Bartlett asks James Talarico how Texas chases “equality” without chasing off figures like @ElonMusk.

Talarico’s answer: Musk’s net worth is a “spiritual sickness,” and the rich should pay something closer to the 1950s rate of 90%.

BARTLETT: “What would you have done to stop [Elon from becoming a trillionaire]?”

TALARICO: “We at one point in this country, we had, I think it was in the 1950s, had a top marginal tax rate of 90%. I don’t think it needs to be that high, but we used to have a political system and an economic system that more fairly distributed the fruits of our labor.”

“And I think the thing that really upsets people, particularly about the Elon example, is that Tesla was successful because of taxpayer dollars, right? Tesla got investment from the federal government, which is why it has been so successful.”

CONTEXT: The taxpayer dollars Tesla received were a LOAN from the Department of Energy in 2010. Ford got $5,900,000,000, and Nissan got $1,400,000,000 from the same program.

But Tesla did something those automakers hadn’t. It repaid the full $465,000,000 it had borrowed, with interest, 9 years ahead of schedule, becoming the first automaker in the program to pay its loan back in full.
